title: Agentic Task Homogeneity: Do Multi-Step AI Agents Converge on Similar Action Sequences?

original_idea.title: Agentic Task Homogeneity: Do Multi-Step AI Agents Converge on Similar Action Sequences?
original_idea.problem: As AI agents execute multi-step tasks autonomously, correlated action choices across different agent systems could produce coordinated failures.
original_idea.direction: Design a set of agentic benchmark tasks and measure whether different agent frameworks take structurally similar action sequences.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Agentic systems operating in shared environments are more likely to produce observable real-world harm from correlated failures than passive text generators.
original_idea.relevant_context: AI Risk Repository (2025) added multi-agent risks as a new subdomain. Artificial Hivemind methodology can be extended to action sequence comparison.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: agentic homogeneity is a concerning direction, but the research is more exploratory than directly addressing a known safety-critical issue.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: setting up multiple agent frameworks (AutoGPT, LangChain, Claude agents) and designing multi-step benchmark tasks requires significant infrastructure and expertise.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone: designing agentic benchmarks from scratch and comparing multiple frameworks is open-ended and likely exceeds 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Existing work on multi-agent failures focuses on failure attribution within systems, not on cross-framework action sequence homogeneity. The AI Risk Repository added multi-agent risks as a subdomain, but no study applies the Artificial Hivemind methodology to compare action sequences across different agent frameworks. This is genuinely unexplored, though the scope is very ambitious.
